extracted.intended_audience: referees/reviewers and authors for Development and other Company of Biologists journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy for journal peer review focusing on cross-referee commenting (sharing reviewer reports among referees) and related priorities for referee behaviour and editorial practice. Applies to referees assessing research papers submitted to Development and other Company of Biologists journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referees should focus on two key questions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Referees should focus on two key questions: how important is the work for the community, and how well do the data support the conclusions?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the primary evaluative framework for referee reports, replacing long 'shopping list' style reviews. Referees are encouraged to prioritise assessment of significance and evidentiary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify necessary revisions, not 'nice-to-have's
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should indicate 'what are the necessary revisions, not the “nice-to-have”s'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises streamlined, constructive feedback aimed at what must be done to support conclusions and reach a decision, rather than optional additional experiments or requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve speed from submission to first decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve speed from submission to first decision (ranked top priority in the community survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal commits to actively looking for ways to accelerate processes while maintaining standards; policy choices (e.g., time-limited cross-referee commenting) are designed to minimise impacts on speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce number of rounds of review and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce number of rounds of review and revision (community priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal aims to avoid multiple rounds where possible while ensuring rigorous peer review; editorial commitment to papers at first decision is noted (accept over 95% of manuscripts where a revision is invited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative peer review / inter-referee discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative peer review trial (inter-referee discussion before a decision is made) — ranked highly by survey respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model can help resolve differences, identify unreasonable requests, and highlight overlooked valid concerns; various models exist from cross-referee commenting to more active discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referee commenting: share reports among referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers submitted after mid‑September the full set of referee reports (minus any confidential comments) will be shared among all the referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing may be accompanied by specific requests for feedback from the Editor. The intent is to clarify decisions and streamline feedback to authors; many journals have done this informally for difficult cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude confidential comments from shared reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the Editor will not be shared among referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the non-confidential parts of reports are circulated to other referees; confidential material remains visible only to the Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limited response window for cross-referee comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees will be given two working days to respond to shared reports before the Editor takes a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two working days is intended to minimise any impact on time-to-decision; the Editor may wait longer in particularly difficult or borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors may request specific feedback and may delay decision when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor may accompany shared reports with specific requests for feedback and may choose to wait for input in difficult cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors balance the need for additional referee input against the effect on speed; waiting is discretionary and used when the decision is particularly difficult or borderline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply cross-referee commenting as standard across all papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-referee commenting is to be implemented as standard across all papers (not just a subset of difficult cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many papers may receive no further feedback or have no change to the Editor's decision, implementing the process universally ensures unpredictable benefits are captured when they arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance benefit of additional feedback against impact on speed
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing peer-review process changes, balance the value of gathering additional feedback against consequent effects on speed to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle guided the choice of a limited cross-referee commenting model (short response window) rather than more time-consuming models; applies to editorial discretion in soliciting further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referee commenting helps resolve disagreements and refine requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-referee commenting can 'help to resolve differences between referees, identify unnecessary or unreasonable requests, or highlight valid concerns raised by one referee but overlooked by the others.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as justification for the policy; suggests referees should use the opportunity to clarify positions, retract or modify unreasonable requests, or support overlooked points raised by colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post the name of the handling Editor (optional community preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: 'Name of the Editor who handled the paper published with the article' (community could rank this change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of several potential innovations respondents were asked to rank; not presented as an implemented policy but as community feedback for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post peer review reports alongside published articles (possible innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: 'Post the peer review reports alongside the published articles'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an option respondents might value; indicates community interest in transparency but not an implemented change in this announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind peer review (possible trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: 'Double-blind peer review trial (author identity withheld from referees)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of several models considered by the community; mentioned as an alternative approach but not selected for this policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (possible trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: '“Open” peer review trial (referee identity known to authors but not made public)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among potential innovations; the announcement notes different journals trial different models (contextual information rather than an implemented change here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Network for transferring referee reports between related journals (possible innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: 'Network for transferring referee reports between journals in related fields'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in ranked options from the community survey as a potential efficiency improvement; presented as a candidate policy idea.
